name: Typescript Best Practices
description: This module captures the best practices for typescript, distilled from common failure modes and what tends to hold up over time.
content:
This module captures the best practices for typescript, distilled from common failure modes and what tends to hold up over time.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Measure before optimizing any typescript bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
2. When typescript guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
3. Prefer the simplest typescript approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
4. Keep typescript outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
5. Keep typescript changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
6. Before starting typescript work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
7. Validate typescript outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
8. Re-check edge cases relevant to typescript (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
9. Surface known limitations of a chosen typescript approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
10. Prefer explicit, readable typescript solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not silently drop typescript edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of typescript correctness.
- Avoid introducing new typescript abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these typescript guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
